page: Amazon Web Services c5a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor. It features 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local instance storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core and single-core performance across most standard suites. The Geekbench single-core score is 1339.0 and the multi-core score is 7998.0, both placing in the middle 50% tier. However, stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10% with a score of 767.39, while multi-core stress-ng performance reaches an average tier of 6142.7. Memory performance shows a stark contrast: cached small-block reads achieve an average 800.68 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read and write speeds are weak, scoring 37.14 GB/sec and 22.42 GB/sec respectively.

This instance is designed for compute-bound workloads that benefit from dedicated AMD EPYC cores without requiring local NVMe storage or high memory-to-vCPU ratios. It is suited for tasks such as batch processing, distributed analytics, static web serving, and moderate-scale software compilation. For machine learning, it supports small-model LLM inference at average speeds, though prompt processing for 7B models drops to a weak 31.66 tokens/sec. Qualitatively, the c5a.4xlarge offers a cost-efficient alternative to Intel-based compute instances by delivering balanced multi-core throughput at a lower hardware-class tier, despite the trade-off in single-core execution speed and uncached memory bandwidth.

Benchmarks show average multi-core performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7998.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 19648.81. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for multi-threaded, compute-heavy workloads such as batch processing, static web serving, and software compilation, where dedicated AMD EPYC cores are required but massive memory footprints or local SSDs are unnecessary.
